clue.text: Diplomacy bringing in one American historian

indicators.note: the word for diplomacy takes the next piece inside it, as if bringing it in

parts.note: diplomacy is tact
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tactful American scholar of the past is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing in' signals the container. Tacitus was Roman, so 'American historian' is a false pairing: the US is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was the Roman writer of the Annals and Histories, a chronicler of the early empire.

clue.text: Shopper's label about to be crumpled

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: a shopper is a large carrying bag

indicators.note: the label's letters go about the scrambled pair

parts.note: a tag is a label

indicators.note: the letters of to be are crumpled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone out buying has a price ticket that is about to get screwed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' makes OTEB from 'to be'; 'about' is the container signal, not a link meaning concerning. In British English a 'shopper' can be a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a shopper is also a large bag for carrying purchases.

clue.text: Church's one against drink

parts.note: CH is short for church
one is the Roman numeral I
anti means against

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is opposed to alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from Tuscany is an example of a drink.

clue.text: Flower, one left in place, coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means read from bottom to top
the letters for one and left go into the word for place

parts.note: to put is to place
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A bloom with a single one left in its bed starts to sprout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts IL inside PUT for PILUT, and 'coming up' reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring bulb with a cup-shaped bloom, famous in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Classic comedy acts trifling with irony

indicators.note: playing about with the letters of acts and irony rearranges them

explanation.surface: Theatre scenes make light of irony in a comic work.
explanation.walkthrough: Petronius's Satyricon is a classical Latin comic novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Petronius's satirical Roman novel is a classic of ancient comic writing.

clue.text: Movement of The Planets with additional symphonic relevance?

definitions.text: Movement of The Planets with additional symphonic relevance?

parts.words: Movement of The Planets with additional symphonic relevance?
parts.note: Holst's suite The Planets has a movement named after the largest planet, and Mozart's last symphony bears the same nickname, hence the extra symphonic relevance

explanation.surface: A music critic notes a piece that matters both in an orchestral suite and in symphonic history.
explanation.walkthrough: Holst's The Planets has seven movements, each named for a planet; Mozart's Symphony No 41 carries the same planet's name as a nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Holst named one movement of his suite for the king of the gods' planet, and Mozart's Symphony No 41 is nicknamed likewise.

clue.text: Consider God's first appearance in NT book

indicators.note: the letter from God goes in the book's name

parts.note: Jude is a short book of the New Testament

indicators.note: only the opening letter of God is used

explanation.surface: Ponder the Lord's debut in a gospel-era scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes G from God, which 'in' puts inside JUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge is to form an opinion, to consider or deem.

clue.text: See spoilt misbehaving-the antithesis of this?

definitions.text: See spoilt misbehaving-the antithesis of this?

indicators.note: the letters of see spoilt behave badly and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Look at the brat acting up: the very opposite of good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a spoilt child misbehaving shows the opposite of refined courtesy.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal courtesy or etiquette, the reverse of a spoilt child's bad behaviour.

clue.text: Cart with first of the lumber, roughly heaped

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the is used
a rough heap jumbles the letters of lumber into a new order

explanation.surface: A wagon carries the first of the timber, thrown on haphazardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' takes T from 'the'; 'roughly heaped' scrambles LUMBER into UMBREL. A tumbrel carried prisoners to the guillotine in revolutionary France.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbrel is a two-wheeled farm cart, famous for carrying victims to the guillotine.

clue.text: Superstitious behaviour? It's seen in sport as well, though not entirely

indicators.note: the word it is seen inside the letters for sport

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
the word it, with 's standing for is as a link

indicators.note: the word for as well is not used entirely, losing its last letter

parts.note: also means as well

explanation.surface: Lucky habits are common in athletics, though not universal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is the container; 'though not entirely' drops the last letter. RU (Rugby Union) is a common crossword sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Set ceremonies or habitual routines performed for luck, as athletes often do.

clue.text: Dance, granted, showing ternary measure

parts.note: to trip is to dance lightly, as in tripping the light fantastic
let means allowed or granted

explanation.surface: A dance, once permitted, displays a rhythm in threes.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a group of three notes played in the time of two gives a three-part rhythmic division.

clue.text: Regulate borders? Bound to involve military, on reflection

indicators.note: reflection shows a mirror image, so the built word is read backwards
the word for bound wraps round the next piece, involving it

parts.note: bound means tied

explanation.surface: A border authority is required to include the army, after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to involve' signals the container and 'on reflection' the turnaround, making TIMILED before it is read backwards. 'Bound' looks like a verb of leaping but means tied.
explanation.definitionFit: To set or fix the limits or boundaries of something is to control where its borders lie.

clue.text: Historical French figure having a role in book one

indicators.note: the pieces for a role sit inside the letters for book and one

parts.note: the number written out as a word
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A French figure from history gets a part in a novel's first volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the role inside the book-and-one letters, splitting ONE as ON...E. 'Historical French figure' points to Napoleon's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon, the French emperor, bore this family surname, as did several of his relatives.

clue.text: Cheers after animal carrier's brought in fictional animal

indicators.note: the vessel's word is brought inside the word for cheers

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
Noah's ark carried the animals two by two

explanation.surface: Thanks are given once the boat full of beasts has docked with a storybook creature.
explanation.walkthrough: TARKA the Otter is a 1927 English novel by Henry Williamson.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Williamson's novel follows an otter of that name through the Devon countryside.

clue.text: Filth shown by singular operatic character?

indicators.note: making the plural-looking name singular drops its final S

parts.note: Peter Grimes is the fisherman in Britten's opera

explanation.surface: Dirt is displayed by a one-of-a-kind figure from the opera stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' treats the name Grimes as if it were a plural and removes the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrained dirt or soot covering a surface is a synonym for filth.

clue.text: Rich lass untidily putting last of jewellery in case

indicators.note: the last letter of jewellery is put inside the scrambled letters
the letters of rich lass are arranged untidily into a new order
only the final letter of jewellery is wanted

explanation.surface: A wealthy girl carelessly drops the final piece of her jewellery into its box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidily' scrambles 'Rich lass' into CHRSALIS; 'last of' takes Y from jewellery, which 'in' places inside. 'case' is a pupa's shell, not a jewellery box.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa's hard protective casing, from which a butterfly emerges.

clue.text: Edible leaves? Chill soft food, ending with mousse, as stuffing for recipes

indicators.note: the chilled food pieces are stuffed inside the letters for recipes

parts.note: R stands for recipe (from Latin recipe, take), so RR is recipes
to ice is to chill
pap is mushy soft food

indicators.note: only the final letter of mousse is used

explanation.surface: A cook chills a soft pudding, finishing with mousse, as a filling in some dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the old prescription abbreviation for recipe, doubled for the plural. 'ending with' gives E from mousse; ICE + PAP + E goes inside RR.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin edible sheets made from rice flour, used in cooking; 'leaves' plays on sheets of paper.

clue.text: A medicine's given to Tom, suffering a form of schizophrenia

indicators.note: the medicine is given to the cat, so it follows it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a tonic is a restorative medicine

explanation.surface: A pill is administered to a man called Tom who is mentally ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a man's name; here it is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonia, a state of stupor or rigidity, is associated with one type of schizophrenia.

clue.text: Composer in police state

parts.note: a cop is a police officer
a land is a state or country

explanation.surface: A musician lives under a police regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron Copland was an American composer of Appalachian Spring.

clue.text: Beat most of ruse using some eastern philosophy

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them

indicators.note: the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: a trick is a ruse

explanation.surface: Someone beats most of a con trick using mystical eastern wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims TRICK to TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantra is a set of Hindu and Buddhist esoteric teachings; the adjective describes practice drawing on them.

clue.text: Energy supplied by crack kit

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
a crack is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Power is provided by a split in a set of gear.
explanation.definitionFit: To kit out is to supply with gear or provide the necessary outfit.

clue.text: Parisian article about a conflict is not informed

indicators.note: the French article goes about the other pieces

parts.note: une is the French feminine indefinite article, as used in Paris
war is a conflict

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece about a war turns out ignorant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal here, not a link meaning concerning; 'Parisian' marks the article as French.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ignorant of something means one has not been told of it.

clue.text: Responsible pupil, though not precisely ideal!

indicators.note: the word for ideal is not reproduced precisely, one letter shifting place

parts.note: perfect means ideal

explanation.surface: A school monitor, though dutiful, falls a little short of perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not precisely' moves the R of PERFECT one place forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior student given duties of keeping order in a British school.

clue.text: Fix soldiers with a quantity of drink

parts.note: to pin is to fix in place
the TA, Territorial Army, is the British volunteer reserve of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are mended along with a measure of booze.
explanation.walkthrough: A PINTA is British slang for a pint, especially of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial British contraction of 'pint of', usually milk but any pint measure of drink.

clue.text: Say a report should be recalled about Poland's first undiplomatic activity

indicators.note: the reversed phrase goes about the first letter of Poland
recalled read as called back, so the phrase say a report runs backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
a report is a loud noise, like a gun's

indicators.note: just the opening letter of Poland is used

explanation.surface: An envoy's statement should be withdrawn concerning Poland's leading undercover work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be recalled' turns EG A NOISE into ESIONAGE; 'about' then wraps that round P, the 'first' of Poland. 'Say' is the abbreviation eg, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is covert intelligence gathering, the opposite of open diplomacy; 'undiplomatic' is the witty twist.

clue.text: Upset soldiers captured by the old foe

indicators.note: in a down entry upset turns the assembly upside down, reading it backwards
the soldiers are captured inside the old word for the

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
men are soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops taken prisoner by veterans are distressed by the opposing side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured by' makes YMENE, which 'Upset' reverses in this down light. YE is the old spelling of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversary or opponent is a foe.

clue.text: Love in its current form providing a haven

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
as is means unchanged, in its present state

explanation.surface: Affection in its present state offers a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert, figuratively any peaceful refuge.

clue.text: Mostly light sentence having coverage on radio?

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: airy means light, insubstantial
time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A fairly short jail term gets broadcast attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of the word for light; 'sentence' is prison time, not grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: The broadcasting time given to a subject or record on a station.

clue.text: Spend a long time in the corridor

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone whiles away hours in a hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallway or narrow way through a building connecting rooms.

clue.text: Moral stance of French college encyclopedia

parts.note: de is French for of
ency is an abbreviation for encyclopedia

explanation.surface: A French college's reference work sets out an ethical position.
explanation.definitionFit: Propriety and good standards of behaviour amount to a moral stance.

clue.text: Amongst others, copper seizing drug gets honour

indicators.note: the policeman with his drug sits amongst the letters for others

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: the policeman's letters take hold of the drug, enclosing it

parts.note: PC, police constable, is a copper
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Among his colleagues, a policeman who makes a drugs bust earns a commendation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizing' makes PEC and 'Amongst' puts that within the word for others. E for ecstasy and PC for constable are standard crossword abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour someone is to hold them in high esteem.
